reasoning_trace.observation: JIP-26 requests 50,000 JitoSOL from Jito DAO treasury to extend the Cryptoeconomics subDAO (CSD) budget for executing JTO buybacks equivalent to 100% of Jito Network revenue (~$12.5m). Funds go to the existing CSD 4/6 multisig from JIP-17. Includes quarterly reporting and open-source requirement.
reasoning_trace.inference: Treasury outflow to an internal subDAO. Need to verify KPI specificity, milestone bounding, and whether the buyback authority/scope expansion is fully disclosed.

reasoning_trace.observation: Author is 'drnick'. Beneficiary is the CSD operating under the JIP-17 4/6 multisig. JTO holders are the affected group via buyback price linkage.
reasoning_trace.inference: Single proposer, internal subDAO beneficiary, no external counterparty named. Multisig signers themselves are not enumerated in this text.

reasoning_trace.observation: Two figures: '50,000 JitoSOL' (the request) and 'roughly $12.5m' (described as ~100% of Jito Network revenue and the buyback target). $3.2M of historical buybacks is also cited.
reasoning_trace.inference: Direction is outflow from DAO treasury to the CSD multisig. The 50,000 JitoSOL is the disbursement; $12.5m is the buyback throughput target, not a separate spend. JitoSOL/USD price is not stated in proposal text — USD value of the 50,000 JitoSOL is not directly cited.

reasoning_trace.observation: Key Outcomes list 'Vault and JTO Auction v1 smart contracts delivery', 'Monthly TWAP buybacks maintaining revenue-to-JTO price linkage', 'POL research paper with implementation recommendations', 'Strengthened data infrastructure'. No numeric thresholds (e.g., minimum buyback frequency, vault TVL targets, paper deadline, infra uptime).
reasoning_trace.inference: Deliverables are named but not quantified. 'Monthly' is the only measurable cadence. Emit vague_kpi at medium severity — qualitative outcomes without thresholds.

reasoning_trace.observation: The full 50,000 JitoSOL transfers 'upon passage' to the CSD multisig. Reporting is quarterly but disbursement is not tranched against milestones. No clawback or checkpoint condition is described.
reasoning_trace.inference: Lump-sum transfer with retrospective reporting only. Emit missing_milestone at medium severity.

reasoning_trace.observation: Funds are governed by the 'existing 4/6 multisig established in JIP-17'. No new authority, no new signer set, no upgrade-authority changes described. The buyback mandate (100% of revenue) is stated explicitly in the Abstract.
reasoning_trace.inference: No HIDDEN authority change — the multisig and its scope are explicitly summary-mentioned and reference a prior governance act (JIP-17). backdoor_permission does NOT apply. However, transferring 50,000 JitoSOL to a 4/6 multisig with no on-proposal disclosure of signer identities and no tranching is an explicit concentration of executable treasury power. Emit centralization at medium severity.

reasoning_trace.observation: Proposal funds JTO buybacks at scale (~$12.5m equivalent throughput) and references ongoing TWAP buybacks plus future Vault and Auction mechanisms.
reasoning_trace.inference: Buybacks reduce circulating JTO (supply-trajectory change). token_dilution trigger is mandatory regardless of direction. $12.5m relative to JTO market cap is not stated in proposal text; the 50,000 JitoSOL disbursement itself is the bounded spend. Severity medium — material supply-side mechanic without proposal-stated percentage of supply.

reasoning_trace.step: Scan off-chain dependencies and technical risk
reasoning_trace.observation: Execution depends on CSD delivering Vault and JTO Auction v1 smart contracts, TWAP infrastructure, and a POL research paper. Code is to be open-sourced under MIT-style license but not yet delivered. No audit requirement is stated.
reasoning_trace.inference: Smart-contract delivery risk is independent of the centralization flag (different mechanism). Emit technical_risk at medium — unaudited contracts pending and no audit gate cited.

reasoning_trace.observation: Open items: signer identity of the 4/6, USD valuation of 50k JitoSOL at proposal time, audit posture for Vault/Auction, runway math behind 'next quarter', clawback if mechanisms slip, and how 'revenue-to-JTO price linkage' is measured.
Proposal text is concise; appendices, JIP-17 multisig signer list, JitoSOL/USD reference price, and CSD historical performance breakdown are not included.
reasoning_trace.inference: Overall confidence medium. List unreadable sections.

questions_to_ask: Who are the six signers of the CSD 4/6 multisig referenced from JIP-17, and have any rotated since JIP-17 passed?
What is the JitoSOL/USD reference price assumed for the 50,000 JitoSOL request, and how is the DAO protected if JitoSOL appreciates substantially before deployment?
Will Vault and JTO Auction v1 contracts be audited before mainnet deployment, by whom, and is any portion of the 50,000 JitoSOL conditioned on audit completion?
Can the unspent JitoSOL balance be recalled to the DAO treasury if Vault/Auction delivery slips past Q2 2026 or if buyback execution pauses?
How is 'revenue-to-JTO price linkage' measured and reported — is there a specific metric (e.g., buyback $ per epoch / network revenue $ per epoch) the CSD commits to in the quarterly reports?
What is the runway math behind the 'exhausted within the next quarter' claim — current CSD JitoSOL balance, monthly burn, and projected exhaustion date?
